frequency_question: How often does the FOMC initiate a rate-cutting cycle within a window of this duration?
membership_rule: Members are defined as historical 18-month periods since 1955 containing at least one Federal Reserve rate-cutting cycle initiation. Excluded are periods where the federal funds rate was already at the zero lower bound with no room to cut.
provenance_note: claims 46 cases from only 14 named (3.3x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 14 distinct easing cycle initiations identified across the post-accord era, omitting extended ZLB periods where structural friction of rate-setting was legally or practically constrained.
known_gaps: Excludes minor mid-cycle adjustments that did not constitute a sustained easing phase.
skeleton: Total historical months from 1955 to 2024 (720 months) divided by 18-month rolling windows, mapped against the count of distinct easing cycle initiations.
multiplier: 14 easing cycles across approximately 46 valid non-zero-bound operating windows of 18-month duration.
validity_reason: Long-term macroeconomic structural frequency; institutional reaction functions evolve slowly over decades.
